description: This record describes PRIMES, the partial equilibrium model of the European energy system maintained by E3Modelling, through the 221-page description of the model version 2018 published on the company's website. PRIMES gives detailed projections of energy demand, supply, prices and investment for each European country and for Europe-wide trade of energy commodities, including emissions. It combines behavioural modelling with a microeconomic foundation with engineering detail, solves market equilibrium prices in several markets as an equilibrium problem with equilibrium constraints, and handles investment endogenously with technology vintages and learning. The description covers demand and supply sub-models, including power generation, gas supply, oil products supply, biomass and new fuels, and says the design suits medium and long-term projections up to 2070 and impact assessment of taxes, ETS, subsidies and efficiency policies at Member State or EU level. Access: the description is public; the model and its database are not offered for download, so use is by arrangement with the provider. Caveats: this is a vendor description of the 2018 version, and no validation study or licence is stated. It suits long-term planning and policy optimisation studies of European energy systems, and relates to the TIMES and Open TYNDP energy system models catalogued here.
